author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff and programs can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty, and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case. Naming no specialty leaves both forms as they are today.
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> shows only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list
/vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty in the machine-readable list
matching is on the whole specialty name, disregarding letter case: 'Radiology' matches the stored 'radiology'
a value that is only the beginning of a stored specialty name, such as 'rad', matches no veterinarian
a specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page or machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list, at HTTP 200
an empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if the parameter were absent, the same rule the existing empty owner search follows
without the parameter, both forms behave exactly as they do today
the machine-readable list is exercised by test as a supported surface, not an unclaimed route [REQ-VET-003]
non_goals: free-text search for a veterinarian by name, or for a pet or a visit (NG-9 as narrowed)
prefix or partial matching on a specialty name
filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty
managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: NG-9 narrowed by ADR docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-vet-directory-specialty-filter.md. REQ-VET-003 reinstates the machine-readable veterinarian list as a supported surface; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays retired in the Superseded list and its ID is never reused. REQ-VET-003 needs no production change beyond test coverage, so it ships inside this slice rather than as its own. Out of my write scope: the ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md needs the 2026-08-05 row added.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing paged-derived-query pattern (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith plus OwnerController's blank-normalizing search) to the vet feature package, so no new module, layer, or dependency appears. One question was genuinely new ground and is now recorded: whether a repository query keyed on caller-supplied text joins the `vets` cache. It does not. Filtering belongs in the repository as a derived query, NOT in the controller: the whole-name case-insensitive rule is a business rule, and architecture-principles.md's Web controller row plus its checklist item forbid adding a new one there; in-memory filtering would also force the controller to recompute Page totals by hand. `Vet` and `Specialty` need no change at all - the eager @ManyToMany association the query traverses already exists to render the page. `VetRepository` gains two overloads; `VetController` gains an optional parameter on each route. docs/system-design.md Contracts and Known Defects are updated, and docs/adr/README.md now carries both 2026-08-05 index rows.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived queries over the existing specialties association: a paged one for /vets.html and an unpaged Collection one for /vets. Neither carries @Cacheable; the two existing findAll methods keep theirs unchanged.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter. The controller strips it and treats blank as absent, then selects the unfiltered or filtered query - normalization and delegation only, no matching logic.
vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty through, or page 2 silently drops the filter. The controller puts the normalized value in the model for the template to echo.

REQ-VET-003 is satisfied by naming /vets a supported surface and exercising it under filter; showResourcesVetList already has a test, so no production change is needed for it beyond the new parameter.

patterns.description: derived paged filter query - Page<Owner> findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable); the vet analogue is findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) traversing specialties.name, with a Collection-returning overload for the unpaged route

blank-parameter normalization in the controller - strip() then treat empty as the broadest result. Same rule, different broadest branch: owner search passes an empty prefix, vet filter calls the unfiltered query
@DataJpaTest with an autowired VetRepository against seeded H2 - the home for the matching-semantics tests

risks.risk: VetControllerTests mocks VetRepository, so the case-insensitivity and whole-name-not-prefix criteria cannot be verified there - a stubbed call returns whatever it is told, and the tests would assert nothing real.
risks.mitigation: Split by level: the controller test covers parameter binding, blank-behaves-as-absent, empty-list-at-200, and that the filtered query is the one called; the matching semantics get real assertions in ClinicServiceTests against the seeded radiology/surgery/dentistry rows. The prd-entry file_targets list only VetControllerTests.java, which is incomplete for this design.

risks.risk: Pagination links in vetList.html are built by string concatenation ('/vets.html?page=__${i}__'). Concatenating a caller-supplied specialty into an href is unescaped request-derived text in an attribute.
risks.mitigation: Use Thymeleaf's parameterized link form @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each value. Do not extend the concatenated form.

risks.risk: Spring Data property-path resolution across the collection could surprise on the traversal name.
risks.mitigation: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase resolves specialties.name; if the parser mis-splits, force the traversal with the underscore form findBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase. Do not fall back to a hand-written @Query with concatenated text.

risks.risk: The H2 vet_specialties table declares no uniqueness on (vet_id, specialty_id) while MySQL and PostgreSQL do, so duplicate join rows would repeat a veterinarian in the filtered page.
risks.mitigation: Seed data contains no duplicates and Vet.specialties is a Set, so the join cannot multiply today. If a duplicate ever appears, the fix is findDistinctBy..., not schema change inside this slice.

risks.risk: Vet reads stop being uniformly cached, which reads as an oversight without the reason.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-05-specialty-filter-as-an-uncached-repository-query.md and back-linked from system-design.md Contracts.

notes: Security placement: the specialty is external input at the HTTP boundary. It is normalized (strip, blank-as-absent) and then passed as a bound query parameter through the repository abstraction - no concatenated query text, satisfying the injection row of security-principles.md Realization. No new endpoint is exposed; /vets already existed. The design is deliberately not weaker than the baseline: caching the filtered query would have widened the cache key space from page integers to arbitrary caller strings on an unauthenticated route in a cache with no configured size limit. The pre-existing page-keyed exposure on findAll(Pageable) is baseline and is not a finding here. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: new ADR 2026-08-05-specialty-filter-as-an-uncached-repository-query.md; docs/adr/README.md index rows for both 2026-08-05 ADRs (the carried-over item from the prd-entry notes, now done); system-design.md Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController, a new paragraph under Invariants the rows cannot carry, removal of the Known Defects row retiring the machine-readable route, and a matching line under Settled since the survey. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit. Vocabulary: prose says veterinarian and specialty; Vet is the code short form and Vets is only ever the wrapper symbol.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: SQL injection: the specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived queries findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and (String). Derived queries bind the parameter; no string-concatenated JPQL or SQL is introduced. Consistent with the SQL-injection row of the system-design threat model.

XSS: all five pagination links in vets/vetList.html now use the parameterized link form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link-expression query values and HTML-escapes th:href output, so the caller-derived value can neither break out of the href nor inject a further parameter. The migration is complete: a grep of src/main/resources/templates for the preprocessed __${...}__ href form finds no remaining instance in vetList.html, and the surviving instances (ownersList.html, layout.html, fragments) interpolate integers or fixed fragment names, not this parameter. The ampersand test (specialty=rad%26ology) pins the encoding.

No second sink for the parameter: ${specialty} appears in vetList.html only inside the five link expressions. No th:utext, no th:inline script block, no attribute-level raw interpolation anywhere in templates/. The JSON route does not echo the parameter back into its response.

Cache decision holds. Keying an unbounded JCache 'vets' cache on caller-supplied text over an unauthenticated route would let any caller grow the cache without limit; leaving the two filtered queries uncached removes that vector rather than mitigating it. The ADR states the reasoning and the repository Javadoc carries it at the point of use, so a later @Cacheable addition is a visible regression rather than a silent one.

Unbounded-input assessment: the absence of a length cap on the specialty parameter leaves no material risk on this path. The value is normalized (strip, blank-to-null), never persisted, never cached, never logged, never written to a filesystem path, and never rendered unencoded; it is bound as a query parameter against an indexed lookup over a bounded reference table. An oversize value costs one bounded query, with nothing accumulating across requests.

REQ-VET-003 exposure profile: reinstating /vets adds no data. It serves the same Vet and Specialty fields the already-public /vets.html page renders, under the same absence of authentication that the system-design Security Context records for every route. Making an already-public dataset filterable narrows a response rather than widening the disclosed field set, and the filter accepts no operator, wildcard, or projection a caller could use to reach other columns.
Supply chain: the change set touches no build file and adds no dependency, so it introduces no new third-party code. Spring Boot stays at 4.1.0 per the committed build.gradle.
No credential-shaped material in the diff: no token, password, secret, or key literal in the production, template, or test hunks.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: 78 prod lines in one feature package (VetController, VetRepository) plus vets/vetList.html; no sensitive paths, no build files, no dependency change. The five doc files are wide but inert at runtime, and the one shared runtime artifact is the vetList template, whose five pagination links all changed in the same way.

semantic_surprise.note: The template moved from concatenated hrefs to the parameterized link form, and Thymeleaf's StandardLinkBuilder appends a null-valued parameter as a bare name with no equals sign (verified in StandardLinkBuilder.processAllRemainingParametersAsQueryParams). So the UNFILTERED vet list now emits /vets.html?page=2&specialty on every pagination link, a visible URL change on a pre-existing page that no assertion pins and that the diff's framing does not lead you to expect. Harmless in behavior (a name-only parameter binds as empty string, strips to null, stays unfiltered), cosmetic in the address bar.

test_adequacy.note: Matching semantics are genuinely proven against seeded H2 (case-insensitive whole-name match, prefix rejection, both overloads), and blank-as-absent is proven by verify never on both routes. But no test ever issues a PAGED filtered query against a real database: ClinicServiceTests passes Pageable.unpaged(), and the pagination test stubs VetRepository and asserts a hand-built PageImpl. Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER ManyToMany, so filtered paging over that association is exactly where a count-query or in-memory-pagination surprise (HHH000104) would live, and the suite cannot observe it.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers ran and approved, the roster matches the full battery, and the security and doc approvals are unqualified with substantive evidence. The test-reviewer's approval, however, ships one open fixable finding (mystery literals: PageRequest.of(0, 5) and a total of 7, with totalPages 2 and totalItems 7 restated rather than computed, at VetControllerTests.java:150-155) - approval with a caveat, low weight but unresolved.

scope_deviation.note: Every changed path is claimed: the nine code, template, test and design-doc paths sit in the superseding design-block's lists, and docs/prd.md is the PRD author's own surface. The one design revision was path bookkeeping with no code change and zero build retries after it; no consultations. Folding REQ-VET-003 and the NG-9 narrowing into this slice was the product owner's decision and is recorded in two ADRs.

rationale: Correct and well-tested where it counts, but two residuals deserve a look: unfiltered pagination links now render a bare specialty suffix (Thymeleaf's null-parameter form) on an existing page nothing asserts, and filtered paging is never exercised against a real database over the eager specialties association. Read the template and the paging path.
